A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CGFlow/3DSynthFlow study. All 29 pages of each version, including Appendices A–F, are readable and support comparison after matching relocated material and renumbered tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular-generation experiments on LIT-PCBA and CrossDocked2020, sampling-efficiency measurements, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments, reports revised model results, and adds a scheduling-ablation condition.

M1.justification: The general CGFlow framework remains, but Appendix D.2 substantially revises 3DSynthFlow. GVP pocket encoding is replaced by hierarchical Semla atom-to-residue encoding; attachment-point features are introduced; and the compositional model's nearest-neighbor protein and protein–ligand connections become fully connected.

E1.justification: The same 15 LIT-PCBA targets and CrossDocked2020 tasks remain. However, Section 6 replaces the catalog-based building-block pool for pocket-conditional generation with an Enamine stock pool filtered for drug-likeness, changing the available chemical inputs. Pocket-specific optimization retains the catalog pool.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain the same comparators: FragGFN variants, SynNet, BBAR, both SynFlowNet versions, RGFN and RxnFlow on LIT-PCBA; and Pocket2Mol, TargetDiff, DecompDiff, DiffSBDD, MolCRAFT variants, TacoGFN and RxnFlow on CrossDocked2020. PoseCheck comparator membership is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported state-flow training changes from 100 epochs with batch size 32 to 30 epochs with dynamic batching. The default interpolation window changes from 0.4 to 1.0, and compositional training uses 20 rather than 80 flow-matching steps. Medium/high sampling beta ranges change from U(32,64)/U(48,64) to U(16,64)/U(32,64). These are substantive setting revisions, not merely additional disclosure.

E4.justification: Appendix F.3 adds a 'Till end' scheduling condition, testing continued joint refinement against the retained nonoverlapping and overlapping schedules. Appendix F.2 removes the 10-step condition from the flow-step sensitivity study. The reward-computation, state-space, and PoseCheck analyses otherwise retain their questions and structure.

E5.justification: Figure 5 changes its stated seed count from two to three, while v2 Table 16 says two. The new main-text PoseCheck summary says four runs, whereas Appendix Table 15 retains three. Statistical reporting therefore changes, but these inconsistencies prevent concluding that additional runs actually occurred.

E6.justification: Results change throughout the main and appendix tables. Reported LIT-PCBA synthesis success changes from 53.12% to 68.58%. High-beta CrossDocked results change from Vina -9.38, 62.2% synthesis success and 24 seconds to -9.42, 36.1% and 6 seconds. The headline sampling advantage changes from 5.8 times at 10,000 samples to 4.2 times at 64,000. Revised architectures, settings and sample budgets prevent interpreting these as controlled before-and-after performance gains.

T1.justification: The CGFlow mathematical formulation, sampling algorithm, loss derivations, and Proposition B.1 with its proof remain unchanged. Appendix E.2 explicitly documents previously referenced empirical reward functions without adding a new theoretical result or revising the existing reasoning.

C1.justification: The framework and joint molecule–synthesis design contributions remain. The abstract broadens the claim of state-of-the-art binding affinity on all 15 LIT-PCBA targets to include synthesizability. This extension exceeds the detailed evidence: v2 Table 19 reports 60.0% synthesis success for FEN1 versus RxnFlow's 65.5%.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 adds limited docking-proxy accuracy as an explanation for smaller pocket-conditional gains and emphasizes full 3D pocket geometry as a mechanism. It removes v1's discussion of dataset-dependent synthesis success and consistently strong cross-dataset synthesizability. Appendix F.3 now interprets the added 'Till end' schedule as the preferred refinement strategy.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands architecture and reward documentation, including hierarchical pooling, attachment-point inputs, explicit pocket-conditional reward formulas, the 99,000/1,000 training/validation split, and UniDock's balance mode. Hardware and training-time descriptions change from four L40 GPUs and 18.4 hours to eight A4000 GPUs and 26 hours. Hyperparameter tables are revised, while the explicit inference step-size entry is removed. Code-access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Abramson et al.'s AlphaFold 3 as inspiration for hierarchical encoding and Lee et al. for drug-likeness filtering, and removes the GVP reference by Jing et al. (2021). The broader related-work discussions in Section 5 and Appendix C remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Local rewrites clarify the molecular implementation and reorganize experimental discussion. The separate sampling-efficiency and synthesizability subsections are absorbed into surrounding results, Appendix E gains a reward-function subsection, and acknowledgements are added. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 4 moves earlier, v1's appendix synthesis-summary table becomes main-text Table 2, and a compact PoseCheck summary is added. Figure 5 is replotted with revised axes and corrects 'Lower is better' to 'Higher is better.' Ablation table rows change, and Figure 7 repairs a disconnected molecular depiction. These are localized display revisions.

improvement.justification: The expanded architecture/reward documentation and added scheduling comparison improve reproducibility and support for design choices. v2 also brings the LIT-PCBA synthesis summary into agreement with its detailed table. However, new conflicting seed/run counts and an unsupported all-target synthesizability claim weaken reporting reliability. These benefits and harms leave the net effect on overall paper quality unclear.
